root_cause.text: `l2cap_information_rsp()` in the Bluetooth L2CAP connection setup path dereferenced `rsp->data` for `L2CAP_IT_FEAT_MASK` and `L2CAP_IT_FIXED_CHAN` without checking that the `L2CAP_INFO_RSP` skb actually contained those payload bytes beyond the fixed header, enabling an out-of-bounds read on truncated responses.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds explicit length checks before each access (`cmd_len >= sizeof(*rsp) + sizeof(u32)` for `get_unaligned_le32(rsp->data)` and `cmd_len >= sizeof(*rsp) + sizeof(rsp->data[0])` for `rsp->data[0]`), and the CVE description states that a truncated `L2CAP_INFO_RSP` with `result == L2CAP_IR_SUCCESS` could read past the skb data.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a length check before parsing the L2CAP feature mask from an information response.
intent_record.what: In the L2CAP information response handler, the assignment to `conn->feat_mask` from `rsp->data` was changed to occur only when `cmd_len` is at least `sizeof(*rsp) + sizeof(u32)`. The surrounding logic for checking `L2CAP_FEAT_FIXED_CHAN` remains unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the feature mask is no longer read from the response payload unless the packet is large enough to contain the 32-bit value. This prevents reading past the end of a short or malformed response and avoids using invalid data when processing L2CAP feature information.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a bounds check before reading the fixed-channel byte from the L2CAP information response.
intent_record.what: In the L2CAP_IT_FIXED_CHAN case, the assignment to conn->remote_fixed_chan was wrapped in a length check that requires cmd_len to be at least sizeof(*rsp) plus one data byte before reading rsp->data[0]. The rest of the case logic remains unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents the code from dereferencing or using rsp->data[0] when the received response is too short, avoiding an out-of-bounds read and leaving remote_fixed_chan unchanged unless the payload is long enough.

grouping_result.intent: Add a bounds check before reading the fixed-channel byte from the L2CAP information response.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body clearly shows the vulnerable dereference: `if (type == L2CAP_IT_FEAT_MASK) conn->feat_mask = get_unaligned_le32(rsp->data);` at line 1829-1830. This reads 4 bytes from `rsp->data` without any length check on the received skb or validation that the payload is present beyond the fixed `l2cap_info_rsp` header, matching the root cause of an out-of-bounds read on truncated responses. The fix is not present here because there is no guard verifying skb length or conditional handling for short `L2CAP_INFO_RSP` packets before accessing `rsp->data`.
